action: Disable Windows Script Host where not needed, block scripts from user-writable folders and keep Defender, AMSI and tamper protection on. WordPress owners: patch, require MFA for admins, disable XML-RPC if unused and block PHP in uploads.
attack: T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1558.003 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
exec: Search-result lures aimed at legal teams are a ransomware entry point, and ordinary WordPress sites are being used as the delivery network.
plain: The FBI warns that criminals rig search results for legal questions so lawyers and legal staff download a booby-trapped file, which can open the door to a ransomware attack.

key_findings: Organisations in many sectors are affected, but the main focus is US legal professionals and legal technology decision makers; WordPress site operators are abused as infrastructure.
Attackers poison search results for low-competition, jurisdiction-specific legal phrases and serve a JavaScript loader from compromised WordPress sites behind a traffic filter.
The FBI counts over 1,000 infected WordPress sites as of October 2026, 216 administrator-controlled domains and more than $28 million in linked ransomware payments.
New in 2025-2026 are abuse of WordPress comment paths and use of geofencing and traffic distribution services.
Gootloader is treated as a ransomware precursor, with follow-on credential dumping, Kerberoasting, lateral movement over SMB and data exfiltration.
recommendations: Disable Windows Script Host where not needed, or control scripts with WDAC or AppLocker.
Block unapproved scripts and executables from user-writable locations and keep Defender, SmartScreen, AMSI and tamper protection enabled.
If the JavaScript file was opened, disconnect the device from the network and change credentials from a known-clean device.
Patch WordPress core, plugins and themes, require strong MFA for administrators and disable XML-RPC if unused.
Block PHP execution in wp-content/uploads and keep web and WAF logs off the web server.

summary: FBI FLASH CC-111626-MW (TLP:CLEAR), coordinated with CISA, describes how Gootloader plants pages for niche legal search terms on compromised WordPress sites and serves a JavaScript loader that often precedes ransomware. It counts over 1,000 infected WordPress sites as of October 2026, 216 domains run by the administrator and more than $28 million in linked ransom payments. US legal professionals are the main target.
title: FBI: FLASH warns Gootloader uses SEO poisoning and hacked WordPress sites to reach US legal staff
